## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs

same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

## Objective
- Build a playable browser game inspired by GTA San Andreas, featuring modern-world vehicles, in the empty PlayGround repo.

## Requirements
- User request: "Create gta san Andreas with new vehicles as in modern world"
- No further explicit requirements from the user.

## Decisions
- Use Vite + Three.js with procedural geometry/textures; no external game assets.
- Build a stylized open-world driving sandbox: reimagined San Andreas city, seven modern EVs, pedestrians, traffic, police/wanted system, courier missions, collectible data shards, procedural synthwave audio.
- Third-person on-foot + arcade driving, touch controls for mobile, GTA-style HUD/minimap/title screen.
- Use a neon-showroom plaza spawn with modern cars and a city skyline; the play button is `aria-label="Play"` so automated capture can start the game.
- Keep performance safe with no real-time shadow maps; use blob shadows and emissive/additive glow.

## Work State
### Completed
- Scaffolded Vite/Three.js project (`package.json`, `index.html`, `src/style.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/city.js`, `src/vehicles.js`, `src/player.js`, `src/ui.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/utils.js`).
- Built city generation: 5×5 blocks, roads/crosswalks, procedural buildings/signs, palms, beach, ocean shader, hills, ferris wheel, showroom/plaza, streetlights, traffic lights.
- Built seven modern vehicles (VOLT GT, CYBER X, AERO S, MANTIS R, TITAN EV, NOVA SUV, LUMEN) plus APEX police car, with wheels, cabins, lightbars, underglow, wheel glow rings, fender arches.
- Implemented player character, traffic AI, pedestrians, vehicle enter/exit, driving physics/drift/boost/battery, collisions, mission markers, shards, wanted/police/busted/wasted, camera controls, HUD, minimap, title screen, mobile touch UI, procedural music/engine/SFX.
- Fixed Play button capture name, prevented favicon 404, added minimap circular clipping, removed duplicate/obtrusive hill sign and arch sign, lowered showroom branding, moved showroom floor above sidewalk so its dark reflective surface renders, added floor neon glows, tuned lighting/camera/colors.
- `npm run build` succeeds with only the >500 kB chunk warning. Browser capture runs with zero page errors; screenshots generated.

### Active
- Iterating on visual quality after the latest floor/car/camera/lighting changes; the latest screenshots were just regenerated and not yet inspected.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/shots/title.png` and `/tmp/opencode/shots/game.png` from the latest run; check the dark showroom floor, wheel glow rings, arches, skyline, minimap, and sign overlap.
2. Test actual gameplay via Playwright: click Play, press E to enter VOLT GT, drive, test collisions/mission pickup/shards, mobile viewport (390×844), and ensure no console/page errors.
3. Fix any visual/gameplay regressions, then run final build and capture verification.
4. Optionally add debug hooks (`window.__SA`) and improve car silhouettes/character proportions if visuals remain weak.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game state, controls, camera, driving, missions, police, UI sync, render loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/city.js`: city layout, showroom/plaza, beach/water/hills, lighting, spawn/showcase positions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/vehicles.js`: vehicle models, specs, wheels, lights, labels.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: full HUD/title/mobile UI styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: HUD updates, minimap rendering, touch controls, toasts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: player/NPC character model and animation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural music, engine, SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/utils.js`: textures, RNG, glow/shadow helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: UI markup and title screen.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Vite/Three dependencies and scripts.
- `/tmp/opencode/shot.mjs`: custom Playwright screenshot/test script.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots/`: title/game/minimap screenshot outputs.
- `/tmp/opencode/vite.log`: dev server log.

## Important Context
- Dev server currently runs in tmux session `game` on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Latest `npm run build` succeeded; no page errors in capture. A favicon 404 was fixed.
- Capture auto-start requires exactly one visible button whose aria-label/text matches `/^(start|play)( game| now)?$/i`; currently satisfied by `#play-btn` with `aria-label="Play"`.
- Current spawn: `x:-2.8, z:68.5, heading:Math.PI`; showcase cars at `z:64`, span `x:-17.1..17.1`, group Y `0.30`.

- Player at spawn is ~5.3 m from VOLT GT and the "DRIVE · VOLT GT" prompt appears.

- The hillside "SAN ANDREAS" sign and the arch's duplicate "NEON MOTORS" sign were removed; a smaller showroom sign at `y=3.3` remains.

- Runtime capture also checks a 390×844 mobile screenshot; use `CAPTURE_URL`/`CAPTURE_DIR` or the custom `/tmp/opencode/shot.mjs`, which uses the installed Playwright from `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright`.

The cars appear dark because the lighting is dim and the body materials are physical metalness 0.62, meaning without env maps they reflect mostly black. MeshPhysicalMaterial with metalness 0.62 and no environment map = very dark. The solution: add an environment map (PMREM from a procedural scene or RoomEnvironment) to make metallic surfaces reflect color, or reduce metalness and add emissive tint.

The simplest robust fix: create a scene.environment from RoomEnvironment / or a gradient equirect texture. Since we're using no external assets, generate a small canvas-based equirectangular environment map with city colors, or use THREE.RoomEnvironment from addons (built into three). RoomEnvironment gives neutral studio lighting; could look bright. Better: generate a custom night city env map via canvas gradient + neon spots, then PMREM. That would make car paint shine with pink/blue highlights.

Alternatively set metalness lower (0.3) and roughness 0.4 and add emissive color * 0.08 to keep color visible. Combined with scene.environment, cars will read much better.

Actually R_y(θ): x' = x cosθ + z sinθ; z' = -x sinθ + z cosθ. θ=90: x' = z (0), z' = -x. So the arc originally from +X to -X via +Y becomes from -Z to +Z via +Y. So the half-torus arc is over the top spanning z; that's fine for a fender (top half). Arc PI*0.9 nearly half, ends slightly below the axle. Good.

But the fender is at x=0 center of wheel, and torus tube radius 0.045, major radius wheelRadius+0.06. It will sit in the center plane of the wheel, like a thin fender; from the side view you'd see it as an arc. Fine, but a real fender has width. Could scale x by 2 to widen. The torus after rotation has axis along X, tube cross-section in YZ; scaling x wouldn't widen the tube along X because tube doesn't extend in X after rotation? Actually tube extends around the ring; at the top of the arc (y max), the tube extends in x as well (before rotation, at the top of the ring, the tube cross-section is in the YZ plane with x=0 → after rotation x axis still corresponds to original z, so at top of ring the tube extends in x). Scaling x would fatten the tube along the axle at the top. Set fender.scale.x = 2.2 for width. Let's add.

Wait after rotation, the tube cross-section at the top of the arc originally lies in the plane perpendicular to the ring tangent. At ring top (0, R, 0), tangent is -X, so tube cross-section is YZ; after rotation y=90°, the cross-section maps to... y stays y, z→x. So tube extends in x (width) and y. Scaling x = 2.2 gives a wider fender. Add `fender.scale.x = 2.2`. But scaling happens in local geometry before rotation? In three.js, mesh.scale applies in local space before rotation, so scale.x applies to original x, not the post-rotation x. Hmm, object matrix = T * R * S. So scale is applied first, then rotation. Original torus local x is the ring plane; scaling x would distort the ring, not widen the tube. To widen along world X after rotation, need scale.z before rotation (since local z maps to world x under R_y(90)). So set `fender.scale.z = 2.4`. Then rotation maps local z to world x. Good.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
process.env.DISPLAY = ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
mkdirSync('/tmp/opencode/shots', { recursive: true })

const browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions })
const errors = []

// desktop
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })
page.on('pageerror', e => errors.push(e.message))
page.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') errors.push('console: ' + m.text()) })
await page.goto('http://localhost:3002', { waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForTimeout(1400)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/shots/title.png' })
await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Play', exact: true }).click()
await page.waitForTimeout(1200)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/shots/game.png' })

// drive out onto the boulevard for a gameplay shot
await page.evaluate(() => {
  const s = window.__SA
  s.enterVehicle(s.vehicles[0])
  s.step(1 / 60, 1)
  const v = s.state.activeVehicle
  v.group.position.set(40, 0.02, 96)

  s.renderer.render(s.scene, s.camera)
})
await page.waitForTimeout(120)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/shots/boulevard.png' })
await page.close()

// mobile portrait

console.log('mobile classes', await mobile.evaluate(() => document.body.className))

console.log('errors', errors)
await browser.close()

# PlayGround — San Andreas: Neon State

A fan-made, browser-based open-world driving tribute to **GTA: San Andreas**, reimagined as a neon-lit 2026 West Coast city.

Run the courier circuit, collect data shards, dodge traffic, and outrun the APEX patrol in seven modern electric vehicles — or park the car and explore on foot.

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3002
npm run build    # production build in dist/
```

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move / steer | `WASD` or arrow keys | left joystick |
| Boost / sprint | `Shift` | ⚡ button |
| Handbrake (drift) | `Space` | `HB` button |
| Enter / exit vehicle | `E` | `E` button |
| Look around | drag the mouse | drag the canvas |
| Zoom camera | mouse wheel | — |
| Music on/off | `M` | speaker button |

## Features

- 25-block open city with boulevards, sidewalks, parks, beach, pier, Ferris wheel, skyline, and a neon showroom plaza.
- Seven modern EVs with distinct handling, plus an APEX police interceptor.
- Arcade driving with acceleration, drift, boost battery, headlights, collisions, and vehicle damage.
- On-foot movement with sprint and jump, plus a rideable MANTIS R superbike.
- Traffic and pedestrian AI, wanted stars, police pursuit, busted/wasted respawns.
- Courier delivery missions, collectible data shards, cash rewards, and a live minimap.
- Procedural synthwave soundtrack, engine audio, and SFX — no external assets.
- Responsive desktop and mobile UI with touch controls and safe-area support.

Built with Vite and Three.js. All geometry, textures, and audio are generated at runtime.

Built **San Andreas: Neon State** — a playable open-world driving tribute in the PlayGround repo.

## What’s in the game
- **25-block neon city** with boulevards, sidewalks, parks, beach, pier, Ferris wheel, skyline, and a showroom plaza.
- **7 modern EVs** — VOLT GT hypercar, CYBER X pickup, AERO S sedan, MANTIS R superbike, TITAN EV truck, NOVA SUV, LUMEN hatch — plus an APEX police interceptor.
- **Arcade driving** with boost/battery, handbrake drifting, headlights, collisions, and damage.
- **On-foot exploration** with sprint, jump, and a rideable bike with an animated rider.
- **GTA-style systems** — traffic, pedestrians, wanted stars, police pursuit, busted/wasted respawns, courier missions, collectible data shards, cash and a live minimap.
- **Procedural synthwave audio** and vehicle/engine SFX, no external assets.
- **Responsive desktop + mobile UI** with touch controls, safe-area support, and portrait/landscape layouts.

## Run it
```bash
npm run dev
```
Open **http://localhost:3002** — the dev server is already running.

Production build:
```bash
npm run build
```

`WASD` / arrows — move & steer  
`Shift` — boost / sprint  
`Space` — handbrake  
`E` — enter / exit vehicle  
Mouse drag — camera  
`M` — music

On mobile: joystick, gas/brake, boost, handbrake, and `E` buttons.
